tasks.short: Review the week's lessons, prepare slides and exercises, write lesson plans, show evidence of preparation on request and leave cover work.

steps.what: Teacher reviews the week's classes in the timetable and the method
Teacher makes slides, examples and exercises for each lesson
Teacher writes each lesson plan in a personal planner
Teacher pulls together written evidence of preparation when the team leader asks
Team leader reviews the preparation in a lesson visit or talk
Teacher writes cover work for a colleague when absent

tasks.design: Lesson plans are kept in a short template in the section's shared space in {DOCS}, linked to the series outline and to materials from the section library, so evidence of preparation and cover work are a link, not a new document. The team leader reads plans there by agreement; preparing and teaching stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans lived in personal planners and folders, so evidence and cover work were rewritten on request.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document spaces and templates are standard in schools.
tasks.still_hard: A shared plan space can feel like monitoring; staff must agree how it is used.
tasks.human_edge: Preparing a lesson that fits this class on this day.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; showing preparation stops being extra work.

reach.task: Teach from an absent colleague's plan
reach.learn: Whether shared plans make cover lessons more than supervision.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces with templates and links are standard school tooling.
Staff have consent rights on tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: from weekly preparation to evidence shown and cover work left; teaching is outside.
Input contract: series outline and materials library kept by the section; plan template agreed by the section; fallback is the personal planner.
Team leader time is outside the teacher's savings.
Use of shared plans for appraisal is agreed with the staff section of the participation council.
s3 keeps 70: the template and links remove copying the outline and materials, but the teacher still writes what happens in each lesson.
unknowns: How often team leaders ask for evidence.
How often cover work is needed.
research_questions: Do shared plans change the quality of cover lessons?

incremental.description: Teacher links plans to the series and materials.
Section head keeps the plan template and library tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: plans stay mostly in the personal planner, so s3 keeps 90, evidence is still gathered by hand (s4 at 60) and cover work is written fresh (s6 at 90) (15.6); high: shared plans used as designed (27.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree goals for the year, draft course objectives and outlines from the curriculum, check coverage, get approval and publish.

steps.what: Teacher agrees with the section which core goals the year covers
Teacher reads the national core goals and the method's goal list
Teacher writes objectives per period and the course outlines

loop.input: The year's goals as codes from the fixed list, the number of periods and lessons, and last year's outline.
loop.output: Objectives per period in pupil language and a course outline with topics, lessons and tests.
loop.check: Every objective must map to a goal code whose text it actually reflects; every year goal must appear at least once; lesson counts must fit the timetable; the teacher edits before the outline goes to the section head.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning formal goals into pupil-friendly objectives and a sensible order is writing; a coverage table only checks it.

steps.what: Teacher ticks off goal coverage across the year in a spreadsheet matrix
Section head approves the course outline
Teacher checks the formatted outline before posting: it matches the version the section head approved, for the right year and class
Teacher posts the checked outline for pupils and parents: formatted and posted by hand today, posted from the approved version after the change
Teacher revises the outline after the year's evaluation

tasks.design: The section keeps the national core goals and the method's goals as one coded list in {DOCS}; a bounded step drafts period objectives and the course outline from the chosen codes and last year's outline, and a coverage table is computed from the codes. After the section head approves, the teacher checks the outline against the approved version and publishes it once to pupils and parents in the electronic learning environment ({OTHER}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Goals sat in long documents and coverage was ticked by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft objectives a goal-code check can verify, and a Dutch practice product already drafts activities for a lesson goal.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what matters in a year is the section's judgement; drafts can map loosely to goals.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what pupils of this age must really master and in what order.

ambition.what: Course outlines updated every year from the evaluation instead of copied unchanged.

tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafted objectives; approval stays with the section head.

reach.learn: Whether shared goal codes show gaps and overlaps between years.

evidence.claim: A Dutch adaptive practice product drafts a class activity for the lesson goal.
Among 259 science teachers in English secondary schools, a chatbot plus a guide cut weekly planning by 31% with no quality difference (randomised, independent).
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets education level is high-risk; drafting course objectives is not listed.
National core goals for lower secondary are set in national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing the year's goals to the outline published and revised; lesson planning is outside.
Input contract: coded goal list kept by the section head from the national goals and the method; last year's outline from the section space; fallback is writing by hand.
Section head time is outside the teacher's savings.
No pupil data enters the drafting step.
s3 keeps 65 because the teacher reads and edits each drafted objective for meaning. Posting keeps 50 of s6 and the check before it keeps its full time.
unknowns: How often outlines are rewritten today.
Whether the method's goals are already coded.
research_questions: Does the coverage table find gaps the section had missed?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews drafted objectives and their goal codes.
Teacher checks the loaded goal list for the year.

incremental.description: Teacher notes what to change from last year for the draft.
Section head keeps the coded goal list current.

approvals.approved_version: The course outline exactly as approved by the section head in s5 and checked by the teacher in s6b against that version, published once to the pupils and parents of the named year in the electronic learning environment; any change needs a new approval and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the section keeps last year's outline with few changes, so the draft saves little and s3 keeps 90 (18.4); high: a new outline drafted from the codes (26.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read papers, attend staff meetings, take minutes in turn, do committee work and follow up own action points.

steps.what: Teacher reads the agenda and papers before the meeting
Teacher attends staff meetings and committee meetings
Teacher takes and types up minutes when it is their turn
Teacher checks the minutes and action items before they go out: decisions as taken, each action with the right owner and date
Teacher posts the checked minutes and their action items to the shared action list
Teacher does committee work such as drafting a policy or organising an event
Teacher keeps track of own action points in the mailbox

tasks.design: Minutes use a short template; the minute taker checks the action items, with owner and date, and posts them once to a shared action list in the {PROJECT} tool with reminders, so nobody tracks actions in their mailbox. Meetings and committee work stay as they are; no recording of colleagues is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actions were buried in minutes and e-mail threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared task lists with reminders are standard school tooling.
tasks.still_hard: Meeting time is set by the school's culture, not by tools.
tasks.human_edge: Speaking up for pupils and colleagues in decisions that shape the school.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; follow-up is visible to all.

reach.task: Chase actions agreed in staff meetings
reach.learn: Whether a shared action list reduces chasing.

evidence.claim: Shared task lists with owners, dates and reminders are standard tooling.
Staff have consent rights on tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: from meeting preparation to own actions followed up; decisions themselves are outside.
Input contract: action items with owner and date entered by the minute taker; fallback is the minutes alone.
No meeting is recorded.
Reading papers, meetings and committee work do not change.
Taking and typing minutes is a first write: s3 keeps 85, saving only the layout. Checking and posting the minutes keep their full time.
unknowns: How often the teacher takes minutes.
research_questions: Do actions close sooner with a shared list?

incremental.description: Teacher updates the status of own actions.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes with each decision and each action item's owner and date exactly as checked by the minute taker in s3b, posted once to the staff and the shared action list; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few actions land on the shared list and the teacher still tracks some in the mailbox, so s5 keeps 80 (2.7); high: all actions on the list (5.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose and plan a trip or project, get approval, book, send the parent form after checking it, collect consent and payments, supervise on the day and guide reflection.

steps.what: Teacher chooses the trip, project or guest speaker and its learning goals
Teacher writes the plan and risk assessment for field trips
School leader approves the trip, cost and supervision ratio
Teacher prepares the booking requests for transport, venue or guest speaker: by phone and e-mail today, from standard request texts after the change
Teacher checks each booking request before it goes: provider, date, times, number of pupils and cost against the approved plan
Teacher sends the checked booking requests to the providers
Teacher writes the parent letter and consent slip with date, cost and medical questions
Teacher checks the final parent form against the approved trip plan
Teacher sends the trip letter and form to parents
Parents give consent, medical notes and payment for field trips
Teacher collects paper consent slips, medical notes and payments from parents
Teacher supervises students during the trip or project
Teacher guides pupils in reflecting on what they learnt

tasks.design: A trip plan template in {DOCS} carries the school's standard risks, supervision ratios and checklist. Bookings use standard request texts within the plan the school leader approved. The approved plan fills a parent form with date, cost, consent text and medical questions; the teacher checks it and sends it through the parent app of the student information system ({OTHER}). Parents answer and pay in the app, and a live list shows who has responded; paper slips stay for parents without the app. Planning the learning, supervising and reflection stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consent slips and cash were collected on paper and chased pupil by pupil.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems have parent apps that take forms and messages; payment links are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: Some parents do not use the app; medical notes are health data and need care.
tasks.human_edge: Making a trip safe and memorable, and helping pupils make sense of what they saw.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; paperwork around trips shrinks.

reach.task: Collect trip payments and reconcile them
reach.learn: Whether app payments end cash handling.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system includes a parent app.
Medical notes about pupils are health data under the GDPR and need extra care.
Parents and pupils have consent rights on rules for pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing the activity to reflection; school-wide events are outside.
Input contract: standard risks and ratios set by the school leader; parent responses entered by parents in the app; fallback is paper slips.
Input contract for s9: about 70% of parents use the parent app; s9 is priced at that share.
s7 saves printing and handing out letters for parents who use the app.
Parents' time is shown in s8 at share 1 and is about what the paper slip took.
School leader and parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
Supervision and reflection do not change.
s2 keeps 70 because the teacher still writes the trip-specific plan and risks; the template fills the standard ones.
unknowns: Share of parents who use the parent app.
research_questions: Does app collection shorten the time to full consent?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the response list and contacts missing parents.

incremental.description: School administrator keeps trip templates and payment links current.
No new ongoing focal work; setting up the trip form is part of writing it in s5.

approvals.approved_version: The parent trip form with date, cost, consent text and medical questions exactly as checked by the teacher in s6 against the plan approved in s3, sent to the parents of the pupils on the trip list; any change needs a new check before sending.

Each booking request with provider, date, times, number of pupils and cost exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b against the plan the school leader approved in s3, sent once to that provider; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about a third of parents use the app, so letters are still printed (s7 at 80) and slips and cash collected (s9 at 70) (9.7); high: about 70% of parents use the app as assumed (13.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The middle school teacher keeps preparing, teaching and leading activities; outlines, evidence and trip paperwork become drafts, links and forms.
skills_to_grow: Keeping plans in a shared space
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose course outlines are renewed each year and whose trips take an afternoon to organise.
